div1.p:
The god of Abraham The fear god of Isaac, & the Strength of Israil. Even the god, & father, of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. Hose:11:3 Taught me, whilst I was yet young, he taught me to goe, leading me by the arms in footsteps as yt I knew not,( yet knew I not that he lead me),But after when more of Age he taught me Step by Step, how I Should walke, In a Child like obedience to his [manicule]divine Atributes with large leadings in his mercyfull nature - love; and gave me large Experience, of his Mercyfull. love, & to greatly to accquiesce. In all his wise dispensations, teaching me, that his wisdom, knew wt was best, & his Fatherly love was so great, as all should work togeth.Rom:8:28: [manicule] for good, to them asyt love him & are Called, or purposed there unto; And altho his teachings, I for many yeares Concealed it, & so Intended; yet since Collecting, what use it might be for my Self & others, I was much Pressed upon in Spirit, to write it downe,(& since by some others) for the bett. Reception, of what furthder manifestation, ye Lord now in these later dayes has declared to me (yet not for my Self only, but for others also, therefore not willing to hide it in a Napkin, well knowing that ye Same Spirit as lead me, is but one spirit & will teach all yt doe but Adhere thereunto, for god, is the same as he was yesterday, today, & so for Ever, who at Heb:1:1: Sundry times, & in divers manners, Spake unto ye Fathers ye Prophets, hath now in these last times spake to us by his sonne whome he hath made heire of all things, putting althings under him, spoiling all Principalities &
This page is blank.
Heb:2 8& powers. for, in that he put all in Subjection under him, he left [manicule]nothing yt is not put under him, but now we see not yet all things put under himbut we see Jesus, Crowned, with glory & honour yt at the name of Jesus, the Saviour, yt Saveth his people Phil:2 10-11 from their sins, every knee; all homage glory & honour & Obedience, of things in heaven & things in yt Earth & thingsunder ye Earth, %to whom be glory & honour %and every tongue shuld confesse that Jesus is Lord to ye glory of god the fatherdominion & praise now, henceforth, &Eternally:(& as I have said)I was Taught when I was young; ye boughs when young & tender, will yeild Easily, So it is with ye tender Soule befor it growes old in Sin, & surely as the first fruits & firstling of the flock god Required should be offerred & sacrificed to him, so is the First of our age & as it is the most acExceptable to god, so it is most easie to man, haveing not Such loads of guilt. If the Accuser About ye tenth year of my ageshould Attempt, to Awaken: it is I say much easyer, yet not all easy.

[four dots in diamond] it was not any perticuler sin: But as all sin: yet remembered none. but a strang frame to have killed my self.For about ye tenth yeare of my age, I found somthing to Awaken a sense of ye Naturof Sin,[four dots in diamond] evento dispaire of mercy which alas or at least to Question whetherI Could Expect mercy,(which alas noe, not man in the gall, but it is himself, in man, his breath [manicule] Gen: 2 vr:7[manicule]of Liveing soule, as he Comes to bring up, throughew, & from ye fall) but soone was stayed with davids praising god, in 30 Psalm:1:2:3.(I will Extoll ye O Lord)In heareing A Sermon onf it, so yt my Sorrow Echoed Joy; yn in another Sermon I Learnt watchfulness at all times,(least Satan Should get Advantage over me) 2: Corin: cap: 2: vps: 11Even to watch ye use of things, lawfull, or any appearance of Evil; all wch I still Acknowledg, First from god, Secondarily much was sucked in from, pious parents, & Religious Education, wth which by Precepts and Examples, I have accustomed my Self to pray: (& About ye 15th yeare of my ye 15 yeare of my ageage, for my Incouragement thereunto: I atained by Prayer, a promise to [manicule]Answer yt prayer: Declairing to me how, & by what Efects, I should know [manicule]yt, that prayer Should be Answered, which was fulfilled at its Apointed [manicule]Season; & haveing had such Experience, how god hath heard & in heareing answered; it did for the future Incouraged me, in all ye Pressurs of my soule to power qout my Request unto him, who has Required it, yt we should Call [manicule]upon him, in the day of trouble, & hath also Promised he will deliver, & wee must then gloryfy him, & wee doe best gloryfy him in Beleiveing unto [manicule]Obedience. And About the 18th yeare of my age Seeing the Strict Practice 18 yeareof some, it much Awakened in me a Serious Search, how it was with my Soule, & to what end I was borne, & to wot End I ought to live, & finding Little to Accuse my Self of sins of comission, I inquired into sins of [manicule]Omission, & in Scripture Record, I found that Danieldavidniel Prayed three times A day Danill: 6: vr: 10:13& david said Seaven times A day I praise three (which Certaine number mayThessalo Chap 5 16:17:18Signified many times, in ye Thessalonians.: it is said Rejoyce in ye lord Always pray wthout ceasing but Psallms: 119 164: vr.I thought it only Referred to set times, which accordingly (with all privasie), Yet dou I thi as David prayed seven set times a day for so he sems to menshantion Eving & morning I prevent ye night waches: ps: 119: 14 at mignigt will I arise & praise ye 119:26. I prevent ye dawning of ye morning. psa: 119: 147:&c.I begun, but my mouth was Stopped, like one Struk dumb, wch [manicule]Caused great consternachan, & terror, Saying within my Self, have I so many Sins, & Can I beg pardon for none, & so many graces doe I stand in neede of & is there not any one grace I Can ask for; yet still did I remaine as one Stupified & dumb, but filled with an awakened horror & greif, even to High despare, which soone was stilled, with an Inward Reflection, I [manicule]was nothing & Could doe nothing, not think in my heart to god, without divine Asistance, &, his Asistance makes our AcExceptance.

Severall disturbing objections, but still I was Answered to study duty, rather [manicule]then Reward, teaching me that tho: I Could not Read his secret will whether he would save me, yet I Could Read his Revealed will wch was that I should serve him; & so in his Strength I Resolved to throw my self on him, in the simple, sincere, Childlike obedience, & I If I perished it should be in so doing, which Reminded me of the 2 Kings Chap:7: v: 4:men that went into the Camp of the AssSyrians; If they set there at the gate they see nothing but death, Attend them: & If the Assyrians saved them alive they should live, & If they killed them they Could but dye. this then was my Cause, & these words waeres my Instructer & good was that god; like an Anchor of hope, to help & draw this to him.

[manicule]I Continued, praying hearing and Reading, but often was the Returne of Sorrows, least I should labour in vaine, & little was applyed byto me, from A Sermon or Reading but Repoofe,(thrugh the Awakned Scence of Sin) as If he spake it to none but me, putting far off all Comfort.

And in some fen-months I was seized by sickness, & something dangerous, as for my owne parte, (Being before A stranger to to sickness) I did not Question but I should dye, which Caused me to mourne & weep to them wth me telling them, I had noe Asurance of a Better life, & now I feared I was to dye, for I had lived 18 1/2 yearsLong time in sin. (Being About Eighteen years & a half ould) yn Some of them said to me that I had been well Educated & in all sobriety brought up, not knowing nor so much as heard of the vanities that most then walked in; I Answered it is trueew I have been well Instructed & did Practice, what I was Capable of; when I was A Child I did loved to pray with my Sister, and to heare her pray & I did like to Read good bookes & ye Bible, as for other bookes I thought it not worth my Time &paines. & I said further I knew not any one sin yt I Lived in [manicule]& this was some stay, but it soone went off, & I said all this is nothing, I did but like a Child, little understanding what I did but o my sins are very many.

A few dayes after this: all my sins were laid before me,yet noe won perticuler sin remembered that all the sins of my whole life was like one act of sin, & that hell was the Receve me, & the hottest place I said, I had deserved, & I see like hell opened to me: A great, black darck pitt, & I at the brinck Ready to goe in, & I [manicule]ackknowledged to the lord, that he was very Just If he did Cast me in & also that he was very mercyfull in keeping me out so long, In the Land of the liveing, I Concluded and said that now hell was my portion, & god was to be praised for his long forbearance to the [manicule]Children of men, for he had been a Just god If he had Cast me into hell as soone as I was borne, for I had been Conceived in Sin & be Brought forth in iniquity: And as the lord taught me he was just & mercyfull, so he made me, to Consider his power \\ Horabellwhether he was not able to save me out of this\\ pit, tho I had deserved it, I did veryly beleive god was able to save me, tho. I was at the very Brinck of hell, Just agoeing in, but whether [angled ladder] it wasgod was willing to save me, this I feared, & thus Continued, A day or two; then It[angled ladder]wasthe lord Answered me that If he was not as willing aswell as able none would have been saved, for it iwas only by
By free grace that we are Saved, & how dost thou know but god will save thee,(I said who(?) me? yes thee, I said I have nothing that is good in me, a poore sinfull Creature, what is there in me, yt god should pardon me, then I was Answerd it is true nothing is in thee, but the lord spake with power, I will [manicule]have mercy, because I will have mercy, & because mercy pleaseth me, & I have pardoned they sins freely, & will Remember them nomore, most gladly did I Receive this word: it put more joy& gladness in my heart, then they when there Corne & oyle & wine Increaseth, & as before I sawee like hell open for me, [manicule]so now I see the heavens open, & an angell in the heavens Ready to Receive me, I had some Questioning of this, how I Could Expect such Mercy as this, being not worthy, I was answered if god stayed to shew mercy till we were worthy to Resceive, we should never have Mercy. Some Objections to the like purpose, but all were Answered, & so [manicule]Answered, as never to Question his love, nor the tempter Could never set footing to disturb my peace, & Comfort never since, but once I said wn sin wrestled within methe woman, as Esau & Jacob I tooke up Rebekah's speech. If it be so why am I thus, If the lord hath pardoned [sideways ladder] to mack me s speake: unadvisedly tho: not sinfulyme, & graciously Exaccepted me why, then, doth sin still strive to over-[manicule]-come me,[sideways ladder] then I have looked back or calling to mind how god Came in by A mighty hand & strong arme, & Pulled me out of the Clawes of Sathan & Brought me from the gates of hell,(the way to heaven is by the gates of hell. Andthen considering, how the lord spake peace & scilenced all my doubteings % & such lick these reme[m]ar maid, my sperit say: it is so, tho I am thus: & how he freely Exaccepted, & as the Raptures as I then had,% & how willing yea even long to be with Xt which was best of all, to see that Xt which I had now but a taste of, to see him face to face: but had some desire after this to live to Gloryfy god that I might shew forth his praise yt had done so much for me, but the lord told me he was all glorious in him self, & needed not any Creature to set forth his glory, then I thought what was I, god had many in the world that he Could make use of to set forth his glory to declare it to the world though I might be called out of it, & I I said ye Lord hath Carried me one from Heb: 13:18 39:Psal:7:42 Psa:2:-strength to strength &a as he hath begun a good worke, & hath gone one so hee & will prosperPerfect it to ye Day of Redemshan he is the same, yesterday, today, & the same forever.

And now lord what wiat I for my Expectations is from thee, my soule Longeth for thee, for the liveing god when shall I come & appeare before god, O the wicked mens dread, thay Call for the mountains to fall one them, & the hills to Cover them, but o the sight of god is the heaven of heavens, those that waite & Expect such things as these what manner of men & women ought we to be In all godlyness & honnesty; how Exact In our words, lay a watch on our lips put A Bridle to our tongue y wee sin not with our mouth, how should wee as Christ, goe About doeing good, when god hath Converted strengthean ouer Bretheren we should Communicate of our Experience to others, we should not want grace by this, but wee should Increase our graces, noe Company but leaves loath some; some savor of good there , strive to season it, O ye sins of omission [manicule]how hard it is not to be guilty of Omitting Duties, as is Required of Every man, In there severall stations And Conditions, besides the duties we Omit between god & ye soule wh[e]n as it is our duty, nay it is our Privaledge & happyness, as god will heare & ExAccept o[ur] prayers that he should let us
us Converse with him And meditate one him, that he will permit us to fetch A turne in heaven, and thatevery day that we may be in heaven by meditation as it were before our time, that we may receive the first fruits of our spirituall Caanan, in this life:Psal. that in keeping gods Commandements there is great Reward, even [manicule]in this life, as well as Eternal Hpapyness, & Injoyment of god for ever, after this life, (nay the Comfort a Child of god Injoyes in this life, in god; will make Amends for any Afflictions he undergoeth for god, but that he will give them Eternall mercies, forver where there shall be no End, but they shall praise god to the longest line of Eternity:
O the height of this mercy O the length, O the breadth & depth of Xt love, who is able to Comprehend it, to know the love of Christ, as passeth Knowledge.

Thus for ten yeares or more, I was lead as in a Land of love being much accompanied with Joy & peace, & often in meditations: as I was Carried forth, to various subjects, somtimes of the love of god, sometimes of the vanitie of the Creature, othertimes meditated of the unsutableness of all things of this world, so Could no wayes be satisfieding to A heavenly desireing soule, & sometimes & the most usual meditations & Admirashaneing, was of the love mercy & pitty of god to fallen man, so that I was, as one yt Could see nothing but love, & in all Could desire nothing but to be swallowed up in him & to be taken to him, which earnest desire was hard to be subdued; to be Contented to wait my Appointed time till my Change Come. [manicule]Many great & Eminent answers of Prayer) scarce anything as ever Asked in prayer; but was Answered he never gave me A desire to ask but hee alwayes had a hand to give, & answered what he would doe[manicule] & I did often know when I should not ask by being straitned and Could not; so that by freedome to prayer, or a Restraint not to pray, I knew his will: & all tho. I found it my dutie to ask yet offered up my desire alwayes to his will, not daring to have any will, tho Indeed my Request was all for spiritualls, whether it was for my self or others as for the things of the world, I willingly did not take thought for ye things of the morrow; of this, much might be written, but I foreare. &as I said) About the end of ten or Eleaven yeares, some difficulties I was to pass therrongh, I still beareing up, but after In some time the sorrow prevailed, & I(not haveing skill to stand fast in the Christian Armour) was as one taken out of a land of peace: I felt it at the same houre th:3:1667:4[manicule]even to A minute, how I was taken out of the peace & Rest and Em[m]ediately put into A wilderness, to be tempted where I was to fight my way through, & with the three great Enimies of man, viz the world the flesh & the dievel, & as soone as by faith & prayer one seemed to be weakned, A second did arise up, so that I had noe & as soone as that temptation seemed to be overcome, A third did arise up, so that I had noe time to goe off my watch and Even fainted threwough long waiting, & Wthen I did think, & sometimes hope they were dead, then an unexpected one would Awaken so that at length,(by Experience), when I found A Sweet Calme,[manicule] I knew it was a Cordial before some storm of trialls In the wilderness
Where, the world the flesh & the divel maintained a Continual war [manicule]yet did I never Question my former Comforts, neither was I at all without great teaching, & Joy in god: in vissions of the night when Asleep & some few in the day, which alwayes taught & declared what I was to pass through.

And thus was I Carried on about ten yeares more, & neer the end of the [manicule]yeares I felt some great thing was to be knowne & Injoyed, but I knew not what, & I had a hungringe desire to know further of god, & how I might understand aright, how to worship him, as hee Required, And that I might Rightly, apprehend ye Intercession of Christ for us [manicule]& how, he was our Advocate with the father & how, I should direct prayher to god, therrow Christ, which I searched out in the scriptures but Could not understand, it, as I did beleive, it might be knowne but was Extream, Scencsible of my owne Ignorance, how little I knew of god, & how Ignorant of my self, even as one knowing nothing.[manicule] And as I had neere ten yeares desired a Redeption to my former state, tho: I was much stayed & Comforted; but I found there was greater Interuption in my thoughts then I had, had formerly, & I did greatly press for the dayes of old, saying O that it were as in the dayes of old when the Candle of the lord did shine Round About me when I set under his shadow, with great delight; O when will thou Restore unto me the Joyes & stillness of thy love;

After this for my support, in June the 23th 1678 A Yeare of Jubele was Proclaimed & Proviphesied to me by an angel, or spe iritIn Dream or vision, & after Affirmed by another angel in such a like Dreame, which was s they had said &, at the time performed to me, which was at the End of six months, Being Decem5b:23:1678 But About A month or three weekes before; I was Brought to that, as to [manicule]be fully Contented to take up my Cross dayly if it was his will, being satisfied to wait ye good Pleasure of god, not desireing, deliverence as I often I have all ways found That Contented resignashan is ye nyest way to dilivatansbeforehad done; & I was no sooner Contented, but in three or fower weekes at most, on December ye 23e (Afore mentioned), I was taken out of this wildered place, & put into such A Calme, as is not to be Expressed :5:li:91that as, the very day & houre& meinite of my being set in the wilderness was so plainely felt, & perceived, being so different an air; [manicule]so the takeing out of it was as vissible. leaveing all stormes behind me, & was, as set into a Sweet still haven, & new scences given me, as one not in a body; That I felt my self quite taken out of all disturbances of outward scences & set in a new air, or another Climat, & my scences all opened to have another spirit given me, as was accompanied with new understanding, & as one which had put off an old garment, nay like one uncloathed of this mortall body, & a new body brought forth to manifestation, which Caused great joy, & Admireation, much more felt then, Can be Expressed, & in a few months after(as followeth,)there opened a view of the heavenly Caanan for which, & for the many manifestations of the Eternal love of the father, threw his son of mercyfull love & Comunicated by his hold & blessed spirit, to which I alone offer all praise, honour, Glory, power, & dominion, of things in heaven, & things in Earth, & things under ye Earth, now to whom be Eternall praise.

div1.head:
A Vision and ATransportation or ManifestasionWhether in the body, or out of the body,(as St. Paul saith) I Cannot tell, but I was often, made scencible, where my body lay, & that my eyes did Abide open, by my spirits Returne to it-
Which was Munday night March ye 17 1678/9
div1.p: Being In Contemplation of mount Zion, & earnestly longing to be in mount Zion state, and also to understand what that Extreame Agony meant which I had been in fowerteen dayes before, (as held me About hald an houre when I was In bed) it was like a dark floud Cast forth, from the dragon, which was Ready to swallow me up, but my Alone defence was prayer, Crying[sideways ladder] out^ & saying nothing Els, for the Crying [sideways ladder]^ wthout ceasinggreatness of my anguish & feare, but O Jesus, O Jesus, hide me in thy wounds, thus for the space of half an houre, till there became a most Blessed & gracious Calme:

And being very scencible, of the difficulty of overcoming, the beast, and great dragon, & to get out of the babilonish principle in our progress towards heaven, my longing grew, still stronger, to be in Mount Zion, & as I was in these desires, I thought, but what If god should Come and Appeare, to me at this Instant, upon which the flesh seemed to Retreat her earnest suit, as ^Imaginingraming to my self that the sight of god was very terrible, but faith soon Choecked these fleshly feares, by Representing that this was the place which I did groan thirst & long for & that still. I was fitted, & made meet for this Inheritance of the saints in light, I earnestly desired some Comfortable prospects and visions of that glory as other have had to encourage me dureing my wandrings in this howling wilderness, this I say I had often pressed after(till, I should Arrive at ye full fruition of the heavenly) to have some Tastes of it, to stay my holy impatience yet at the same time i was Afraid, lest the sight of such a glory: should not make it more difficult for me, to be Content to stay here, in the body & increase my thirst, even to fainting, for the liveing god: these thoughts made me power out my Request, Crying out, o stay me with flagons and Comfort me with apples; for I am sick ofwith love: and sSoon after it being then neare half an hour past Eleven at night. And as I lay looking up (by the spiritual eye of faith), I perfectly deiscserned a touch one the top [manicule]of my head, as drew my spirit out of me as yn draw a knife or sword out of a shape & it cut as it was drawn forth I felt it cut sharp as a fox eged sword And I saw paradice with the tree of life in the midst of it very pleasant, & not to be Compared to anything here below; the fruits that grew upon it were of most beautifull & pleasing Colors, the leaves were of A most fresh and lively green, the grass which grew under it was young & tender, & of a passingpleasant greene, tincture, I Could see no weeds; & all appeareinged as if it had been newly watered. yet, did not this fully satisfie me, Except I might also see ye kingdom of Christ, then was I had up higher, where I saw Jesus in ye appearance of a man, all surrounded with a most glorious light wch greatly transported me, for now, I knew I was Come to the place which I
Had so long desired to be-hold: here I stood Admireing, for some [sideways ladder] My Angell Apeared to me but I underst-nd it not.while; whilst I was here I appeared to my self,[sideways ladder] & after I appeared, as a spark of light, & according to my desire I sometimes mounted up to see Jesus, & then againe descended to paradise, all which motions were verySwift: as the light. After this I desired to see the Father, & after a little stay in the Kingdom of Christ, I was had up to god the father.

but oh! oh! oh! ye beauty! ye Glory! the splendor! the brightness! the Exceeding unexpressible glory that was there! at the sight of which I threw my self downe before it, Crying Continually for Above A Quarter of an houre; my god! my god! I am now Come to the place to which Thou hast, Called me, & which I so long desired to see o I am now Come to Enjoy thee! thee being got Above all those difficulties I had been so long wading through, viz ye Kingdom of the great dragon & Beast with this Babilonish principle I can[n]ot Express the delight I tooke to see my self Redeemed from all those Burthens, lets, & hindrances I had so long groaned under.& I saw the Dragon & the beast and Babylon lye one the Earth, the dragon was Represented of A long shape & of a Green Colour like a serpent, it had fowuer short legs the foremost appeareing the longest, it was terrible to be hold: ye very thoughts of it, since neere made me tremble it appeared like a greay Lion & seemed very eager & fierce, to finde what was become of his prey, but I feared him not, being Extreamly pleased, to see my self so safe, but soone after the beast saw me & fixed his fierce great eyes upon mee with his Jaws wide open, as on watching for the prey which was in his Sight, tho, out of his Reach. The Babylonish principle lay one ye ground, in the appearance of toys & trifles of severall sorts and aspuppets for Children, they were Represented to me as If they had been SpewedSpewedout, & therefore were not to be taken up againe, I desired also to See hell, which I saw at a distance, in the likeness of a dark % o the felt Imbrases of god the father Thee devin loveSmoaking furnace, even a thick darkness which Comprehendded not the light: Then my god told me (as I sate in a Cloud of light & in the embraces of Divine love, that I saw not Come up to Abide there, as yet, but that I was first to pass, the bryers and thorny way, Paradise being hedged about with thornes, & none Can Enter into it but by passing the same, then I looked downe to Paradise, & saw such a stony & thorny way as I had never seen before, being all stones, & no path way to be seen, nor any body walkeing in it, the stones were half as high as my self, some times it appeared all stones, some times all thornes, & those the highest appeared Impossible to pass, I Indeavored to go but Could not tell where to tread, I tooke Care that no long garment might hinder me, I thought I would Enquire of Travellers that went that way to direct me. (tho I saw none) but presently I was Checked with a stay they need a guide themselves; I ecchoed back againe, Lord send thy spirit Truth to guide me I looked very Earnestly, to see whether I Could see any, one, in the same way with me, at length I saw one, whome I knew who Came fore ward, tho. the way was very bad, & up hill, & I saw yt the higher she [manicule]Came the faster she went tho. the way seemed worse, & worse, but at
Last ye thorny way seemed to slide away & disappeare, & instead thereof appeared a pleasant river of glass which Compassed paradise, & paradise appeared; much more beautyfull & pleasant than before, then I desired to see god ye Father againe, & the Elders in heaven with there Crownes & I desired also to sit, with them, with a Crowne one my head, & I did so, & when they fell downe & praised god, I Joyned with them falling downe before ye Throne with great Joy, then I desired to behold Christ Againe, & to see his heart (as some had seen) which I Beheld flaming, with love, to the saints. then I desired to Enter into the heart of Christ, & so I did, Entering in & Comming forth againe very swiftly, for several times; after this i was desireous to Enter into the whole Christ, & presently there upon I was in ye person of Christ, where I felt & saw my self: for I saw my Eye in & threw Christs eye, & I saw my head neck & brest in Christs, as inthrew a looking glass, so I was Satisfied; yet, I desired also to see & feel whether my hand was in Christs hand, & I found it was, & I laid hold of the hand of Christ with my fingers, and it felt to the hand which touched, as if it touched anothers hand, but to ye hand which itwas touched, as if the Right hand touched tooke hold of the left ( apon wch my sperit retorned to my body & I fou[n]d my right hand hand had tuck hold of my left hand, I was much amazed for I did not think I belong to my body or shuld ever a returne to it agane, but sune was caught out of my body more swift then an Arro w:out of a Bow,) yea I saw my whole man in & through the transparent body of Christ, which sight did Cause, un-Expressable joy in me to see yt Christ was one with me, & I one in him, yt Blessed union which I had long, desired, Clearely, to understand. Then I desired to see god the father sitting on his throne of glory wth a Rainbow, ov[er] his head, this was An un Expressible great glory, & Majestie streaming forth beames like a glorious sun, tho: Infinitely transcending [reverse %] orbyt wee see here; in ourye Heavens CircumferenceOrb [reverse %] of which glory there were most beautyfull & lustrous colours, some what Resembling the Colours & Copass of a Rainbow, but far more Beautyfull; all which I beheld with great Joy & Admiration. I Desired likewiss to see Christ in his vesture dipt in blood. then was I im[m]ediatly transported caught up into his glory & I saw his Magestie Cloathed, with a loose garment ye outside of whch was the Colour of pure Blood, but ye Inside was as lined with white, which white seemed to spread it self over most of the Red; some times I was taken up with the Admireing Consideration of Christs love, whilst I saw his love, flaming heart, from which some blood streamed forth, & also severall silver Crystalline streams: after I see the son of god in this vesture of glory Apeare at the Right hand of the Father (who appeared, as before) on his throne surrounded with an un Expressible brightness & glory, & the Rainbow Encompassing all: I desired to see ye Holy spirit which I saw in the Appearance of pure Silver Crystalline streames one the left hand of the father:| then againe I saw the three, Father sonne [manicule]& spirit united into one great glory making one great glorious light, & I went intowith them; together with the Elders, & we were all one great light; & then Againe they Appeared three as before, & the Elders apart & I apart, & I beheld there glory, & then againe I was swallowed up like a smaller light of a greater, & Changed into the same glory severall times, but none Can Expect Expression from me, answerable to those wounders, & glory which there I Beheld they being Indeed
Beyond all Expression. Still Continuing to behold this glory I saw noe Angels, therefor desired to see them, & immediatly there were severall of them Compassing part of the throne, they were like unto transparent gold, with the faces of men, with two large golden wings comeing forth of each side of theire faces which were most glorious, after this seeing these streames come forth from the heart of Christ, as I had seen before like unto transparant silver, I asked what it was, he said it was the fire which was to purifie the saints, then I had a minde to see the wounds of Christ, & I looked one his hand, & the wound there, did Glister like the purest part of the light, which I saw in god the father, Compareing it together: thus I Aboade in this glory & would often go into the purest part of light, of god the father, & be one with the father, & then Come out againe; & Returne as often as I would, I desired to have an Antient Christian of my Acquaintance there, who I knew had for a long time desired to see this glory, yt he might Come & enter into this light, from whence god is Called ye father of lights, & a little aft[er] he Came; then I desired that one of my Children might Come up, & in some little while she Came, & then another, & so till all were Come in, & in the same order as I had desired it, first lightof all my friend entered into the pure ghlife, & then all my Childeren one after another, & as they Came up I Remembred Remembered two little Children, which died, one at 14 weekes the other at 14 dayes End, & Immediatly as soone as I began to desire it, they Came, like two bright sparks one after theanother & Entered into this great light, & be Came one with it, as a spark if swallowed up of the flame, & then Came forth againe (to wit my friend & Children which awre living, in the same order, as they went in (them furst as went in furst.) all severall yet all like one cases of bodys, seeing them altogether, & yet severall, through Each other: Then I desired to see all the saints Come up to this glory, I Contineued in the glory, beholding the Father & sonne, but had not seen the spirit for some time, haveing there for desired to see the saints. I saw them Come like a glorious white Cloud, two & two together thick & Close, a little behinde ye Right hand of Christ, & penetrated Into Christs body, & through his heart Came forth againe, & Entered into the middist of the glory of the father, as wee had before, & so [sideways ladder] them furst as went in:i: all severally yet coming all out threw each other wch was wonderfull.there passed an Innumerable Company, & they still Ascended without Ceasing, till I Ceased to be hold, & then they Came out of the father Againe, in the same order as they Entered in [sideways ladder] & all of them sate downe round the throne, which was then of a very vast largeness, ye Eld[er] & saints sitting Round it; I looked to see whether the saints had Crownes like the Elders, & I saw they had, tho I saw they had none till they were gone through Christ, into the Father, & Come forth againe; & sat downe about the throne;& their Crownes as I thought were all of a size, they sitting in great order; the bottome of the throne was like one Smooth glass, & there were many more angels then, I had seen before, all like the former, Compassing the throne one the backside(as it were)of the saints & Elders(a little above
Theire Crownes)where they might be fully seen.

Then I thought what the lamb was, which St. John speaks of in the Revelat[ions], there stood a lamb as it had been slaine, & I looked & by the midst of the throne, neare the left side, at the foot of ye father there stood as a lamb, with its Right side towards me with A bloody place in his neck, & some blood was upon the woole, as if blood had run downe from the said wound, yet it was alive, Then I desired to heare ye saints Sing, all honor, & praise, to him; that sits one ye throne, Hallelujah, but feareing, I fainted least I should not be able to beare yeso glorious a Melodie, yet hoarkned, & when I Could not heare them sing, my selfsperit sung praises, to him yt sate one the throne, but Cannot Remember it. I still beheld the glory untill it begun to descend nearer, & the nearer it Came ye less, was the light & splendor: I said, the glory is less ye nearer the earth it Comes, or is it not because my eye of faith is somewhat, dimmed; then pressed i with a streaching forewards yt faith might not faile, but that I might see ye glory, as bright as I had seen it; upon thisan, the throne disapeared & was gone & I saw the glory of thefather of lights (the glory farre Exceeding any I had seen before) like to Transparent gold, mingled with a fiery light, which shined downe to the Kingdome of the sonne; & this glorious light shined In great beauty through the Kindom of the sonne, into Paradise below it, as A Reflection of the first pure light, and it became more Beautyfull, but far then before, shedding an unExpressible beauty over all the trees & flowers which appeared all transparent.

After this, there was A sheet of light drawne before this surpassing gloruous & beautyfull light, & another little sheet seemed to descend from it like a Cloud of Light upon the thorny ground, & lay upon it & I saw it as long as I looked after it: It being now neare two in the morning when this last appeared, the whole haveing Lasted about two hours, yebut the Idea of all remained fresh with me, from first to Last.for som dayes togather After one thing was observeable yt nothing of all I desired was denied me, but ye heareing of them sing, which I desired though not without some feare, as I had done all the Rest.

There was towards the End of this vision as I came neerer the Earth A Request put up by me (finding I had nothing denied me) Lord what wilt thou doe with this nation, & straight there Appeared a hand & arme streached out toward them, with a slight moving of the hand twice, looking like the waving or putting by my Request: wth these words, Concerne not your self with that. But oh the Ravishing & unExpressible joys I felt when I sate in the delightfull Embraces of Divine love, a joy which as it Could never be apprehended by me before, so neither Can it in the least be Expressed, by me now, And how it is very observable, yt when god told me I must goe downe Againe, because I was not Come up as yet, there to abide, & I saw the beast & dragon ready to Receive me; I was not in the least displeased, neither found I any desire to the Contrary, or any feare, but found my self wrapt up in a Quiet stillness acquiescing in the will of god, with a great delight, in the present Injoym[en]t, finding my self above, the reach of evils for the present.
Severall things here are set downe, short of what they might have been Expressed, but all infinitly short of any thing that Can be any way declared.

div1.head: Wednesday Evening, June 11th 1679
div1.p: Soone after I was abed^ being perfectly Awaked, I see by thesperits eye of faith, A very pleasant still River, & Abridge went Cross it, riseing in the Middest like an arch, but narrow. I went to goe up onye stone steps as was there to goe one the bridge to A rock, I seeaw one the other side. But when I come neare A Rockto Climbe ye bridge went higher, like a Cloud or Rainbow, so that I see saw it Could not be walked one by a weighty body of flesh, but an AtheAerial body, for the bridge was A Cloud of air[e]Aire then I Contented my self to looke one the further side of the river to the Rock, & I seesaw most pleasant greens, wch grew as If they grew out of the Rock, the Rock was Exceeding high and large, It appeared more plainer to looke like a Rock, but Extream pleasant & beautifull, in great variety, & beauty but seemed like a Rock, but a Rock of wounder, the more I woundered at the Beauty, Aboundantly more Beautyfull it appeared, yet noe great light, but shaded;one the Right side of this Rock, A glorious sun Begun to Arise, but it was so Exceeding Glorious, as I trembled, and Could not Behold, then it went downe, after it Arose alittle againe But I Could not bare it, so it dissapeared, though I had A desire to have borne it, & looked for it, & If I did but looke towards it it Begun to Appeare, as If it did Declare that nothing hindred its Ariseing but my weakness, as Could not bare it, & there by shews his tenderness, to Compassionate our weakness, being in bodies of thick Clay.
